items.title: Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview 2 Brings Browser-Based Gaming To Blueprint-Only Projects, Enables AI Workflows By Default And Improves Rendering
items.summary: Epic Games has released Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview 2, introducing significant improvements to browser-based gaming, AI-assisted development workflows, rendering, animation, and cinematic production. The latest update expands upon the initial Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview, which introduced experimental WebAssembly and WebGPU support alongside several AI-powered development tools. According to Epic Games' official release notes, one of the biggest changes is that developers can now package Blueprint-on

confirmed_facts.text: According to Epic Games' official release notes, one of the biggest changes is that developers can now package Blueprint-only projects for web browsers without adding C++ classes.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: According to Epic Games' official release notes, one of the biggest changes is that developers can now package Blueprint-only projects for web browsers without adding C++ classes.

confirmed_facts.text: Meanwhile, Unreal Engine 5's AI agent toolsets are now enabled by default, making AI-assisted development more accessible directly from the editor.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile, Unreal Engine 5's AI agent toolsets are now enabled by default, making AI-assisted development more accessible directly from the editor.

confirmed_facts.text: Interestingly, the update also includes some substantial improvements to cinematic rendering workflows, with Epic claiming an approximately 30-fold speedup in a particular Movie Render Graph operation.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Interestingly, the update also includes some substantial improvements to cinematic rendering workflows, with Epic claiming an approximately 30-fold speedup in a particular Movie Render Graph operation.

items.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.

confirmed_facts.text: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland - Published A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland - Published A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said.

confirmed_facts.text: The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard.

confirmed_facts.text: It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia.

confirmed_facts.text: Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday afternoon that fire was no longer visible from the outside but thermal cameras showed that some containers on the ship were still warm.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday afternoon that fire was no longer visible from the outside but thermal cameras showed that some containers on the ship were still warm.

confirmed_facts.text: The Sparta II was "slightly listing", Finnish authorities added, but the "situation is stable" and no fuel or other "hazardous substance leaks" had been detected.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The Sparta II was "slightly listing", Finnish authorities added, but the "situation is stable" and no fuel or other "hazardous substance leaks" had been detected.

confirmed_facts.text: Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones appeared to have been used in the strike and that there was "no threat" to his territory's supplies.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones appeared to have been used in the strike and that there was "no threat" to his territory's supplies.
